**Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition** [@dantzig1960] targets problems made of independent
blocks tied together by a few *linking constraints*. It rewrites each block as a convex
combination of its extreme points, keeps only the linking constraints in a *master
problem*, and generates the master's columns on demand by solving one pricing problem per
block. The column-generation idea goes back to the multicommodity-flow computation of
@fordfulkerson1958 and the cutting-stock method of @gilmore1961. Inside branch-and-bound
it becomes *branch-and-price* [@desrosiers1984; @barnhart1998].
